summary: the set's only `@fail` without `__RESET`: after one rejected sequence every later event of the binding re-raised KEYPAIRGENERATOR-ORDER-00. REPAIRED at gh105 task 9.2
reason: EVIDENCE: BEHAVIOURAL, recorded and not repaired (gh105 task 8.7, review finding W2). Without the reset the monitor stays in the failure category after the first rejected sequence, so every later event of the same binding re-raises KEYPAIRGENERATOR-ORDER-00: one wrong call sequence is reported as many. The `kp = null;` this change wrote into the block (hunk ee86d177e08f, tasks 7.5 and 4.14) replaced an `ExecutionContext.instance().remove(Property.GENERATED_KEY_PAIR, kp)` and did not add the reset; it also clears `kp` while leaving the sibling field `algorithm` set, so the field the acceptance-point handler stages and the field `validate(keySize)` reads are cleared on different schedules. The sibling KeyGeneratorSpec.mop:163-169 does both -- nulls its two staged fields and resets -- which is what makes this an asymmetry rather than a house style. Repairing it is a behavioural change under decision 7: it changes how many reports a rejected sequence draws, and that needs its own corpus measurement, which this change did not make -- it measured where predicates are read and written, not the cardinality of ordering reports. The repair belongs to whoever revisits KEYPAIRGENERATOR-ORDER-00 with a corpus in hand; what is owed here is that the asymmetry stops being invisible. REPAIRED (gh105 task 9.2, 2026-08-25). The `__RESET;` is in the block and the asymmetry is gone: 21 of 21 `@fail` handlers reset. Two things the repair does not claim, both measured on the day it landed. First, `ErrorCollector.addError` dedups on (spec, code, event, class, method, location) -- a `HashSet` in rvsec-logger-logcat/ErrorCollector.java:51-54 -- so 'one wrong call sequence reported as many' was true of the *emissions* and never of the rows: the observable delta is at most one row per distinct call site, and it comes from the condition-false dispatches, which take no transition and so never recompute the category that made the handler fire. Second, the corpus measurement this row said the repair was waiting for was not made and is not what licensed it: the differential harness returns 159/159 traces `unchanged`, `KeyPairGeneratorSpec-sticky-fail.txt` included, because the TraceRunner gives every dispatch one synthetic call site. The evidence is the generated monitor's `reset()` clearing the flag and this row, which is why task 9.2 sits in the block that needs no researcher decision: no program changes what it is accused of. `kp = null;` still clears one staged field while `algorithm` stays set -- the asymmetry with KeyGeneratorSpec.mop:169-176 that this row also named -- and that half is untouched.

summary: the pinned expert copy adds CCM to the AES modes; upstream never carried it
reason: The audit measured the three local copies of the 49 rules. The upstream CogniCrypt checkout (Crypto-API-Rules, master at 6d844ab, 2022-05-12) and rvsec-cognicrypt/CrySL-Rules are byte-identical; the pinned replication-package copy differs in exactly one value, adding "CCM" to the AES modes of Cipher.crysl:97,113. summary: SSL resolves to the same implementation as TLS on API 30 and is accused anyway
reason: Conscrypt android11-release OpenSSLProvider.java:80-81 registers SSLContext.SSL and SSLContext.TLS on the same class, classOpenSSLContextImpl + defaultSSLContextSuffix, where the suffix is the TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3 one. So the 103 SSLContextSpec/SSL events of the published corpus did obtain a TLS context at run time, and this row exists so a reader of a report knows that. The value is accused all the same (researcher decision, 2026-08-24): the registration is a `put`, not an Alg.Alias, so INV-INS-127's alias rule gives it no row; SSLContext.crysl names TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3 and nothing else; and asking a provider for "SSL" is the misuse the rule is about, whatever this one platform happens to resolve it to -- an app carrying that string is one provider or one API level away from a real SSLv3 context. Contrast the TLS row, which IS a platform-value: TLS is the name the platform documents and the one an app wanting the current protocol is told to ask for.

summary: HMAC-SHA256, HMAC/SHA256, HMAC-SHA384, HMAC/SHA384, HMAC/SHA512, HMAC-SHA512 duplicate three expert entries

These entries have a clause behind them -- they are the frozen jca's own spellings of an expert entry, and the set's normalisation rule (case folding plus the alias table) already makes the expert entry match every string they would. They are kept rather than stripped for the reason D-15 gives: they change no verdict, so removing them is an unvalidated edit that can only cost, while keeping them cannot. The six entries above are the frozen jca's spellings of the last three; the KeyGenerator rows of alias_table.csv carry the same six against the same canonical names. AMENDED, gh109 task 6.3: the general sentence above -- that the normalisation rule "already makes the expert entry match every string they would" -- is FALSE FOR THIS FILE, and the six entries are LOAD-BEARING rather than redundant. `matches` resolves an observed name through the alias rows of the SERVICE it is given, and this file calls `ConscryptAliasTable.matches("SecretKeySpec", ...)` (`:105`, `:166`). There is no `SecretKeySpec` service in `alias_table.csv` -- the twelve services it carries are AlgorithmParameters, CertificateFactory, Cipher, KeyFactory, KeyGenerator, KeyPairGenerator, Mac, MessageDigest, SecretKeyFactory, Signature and TrustManagerFactory -- so `canonical` returns the observed string unchanged and only the case fold applies. `HMAC-SHA256` folds to itself and does not fold to `HMACSHA256`: the separator survives. Strip the six and the specification stops admitting exactly the spellings the frozen `jca` admitted, which IS a verdict change. The `KeyGenerator` rows of `alias_table.csv` do carry the same six, and they are why the sentence reads true for `KeyGeneratorSpec`; they are not consulted here, because the service name differs. The entries stay, and now for the reason that holds.
